security_advisory.detail: The UC San Diego research that broke KARR/SWDS also flagged Rockledge devices as vulnerable, but harder to attack: rather than one universal key, an attacker must intercept and replay the digital exchange between the app and the device. The vendor had not responded to the researchers' disclosure at the time of publication, and there is no known fix. This is a reported, not-yet-independently-confirmed concern — worth knowing about, lower certainty and harder to exploit than the KARR case.
security_advisory.summary: Reported Bluetooth weakness — an attacker who can intercept and replay a live exchange may be able to control the alarm.

credentials.notes: No credential crosses to this app; it never connects.

factory_reset.effect: Not applicable — this app never connects to or configures the device, so it has nothing to reset. Any real reset is done at the device.

methods.description: Passive: the device advertises over BLE, we match the name and warn. No connection is made.

setup.notes: Nothing to set up: this app never connects to the device. It recognises the BLE advertisement and warns; the match is inferred from the advertised name (see testing.notes), hence low confidence.

rejoin.notes: Recognised on sight wherever it advertises; nothing is stored.

testing.notes: Not hardware-verified. The advertisement match (BLE local name starting "Rockledge") is inferred from the product name; the exact BLE name/UUID is not public. Low-confidence, WARN-ONLY.
